tool.name: Cyclospora PART haplotype caller
tool.description: Per-PART amplicon haplotypes from one marker-aligned BAM
tool.command:
@SCRATCH@
## Specimen id: the explicit text wins; otherwise the collection element ## identifier, with a trailing .bam removed so a collection of BAM files does ## not put ".bam" into column 1 of the sheet. #set $eid = str($input.element_identifier) #if $eid.endswith('.bam') #set $eid = $eid.rsplit('.bam', 1)[0] #end if #if $specimen and str($specimen).strip() #set $spec = str($specimen).strip() #else #set $spec = $eid #end if
case '$spec' in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) echo "specimen id '$spec' is outside [A-Za-z0-9_.-]; set 'Specimen id' explicitly" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac &&
## pysam needs the index beside the BAM under the name it expects. ln -sf '$input' 'input.bam' && ln -sf '$input.metadata.bam_index' 'input.bam.bai' &&
#if str($reference.source) == 'history' ln -sf '$reference.markers' 'markers.fa' && ln -sf '$reference.parts' 'parts.bed' && ln -sf '$reference.known' 'known_haplotypes.fa' && #else ln -sf '$__tool_directory__/refs/markers.fa' 'markers.fa' && ln -sf '$__tool_directory__/refs/parts.bed' 'parts.bed' && ln -sf '$__tool_directory__/refs/haplotypes78.fa' 'known_haplotypes.fa' && #end if
python '$__tool_directory__/part_haplotype_caller.py' --bam 'input.bam' --markers 'markers.fa' --parts 'parts.bed' --known-haplotypes 'known_haplotypes.fa' --specimen '$spec' --min-span $gates.min_span --min-freq $gates.min_freq --min-reads $gates.min_reads --out '$calls' #if $emit_summary --summary '$summary' #end if

param.name: input
param.label: Marker-aligned BAM
param.help: Coordinate-sorted BAM of one specimen aligned to the marker FASTA, already filtered to MAPQ >= 20 proper pairs. This tool does NOT re-apply those filters. Map it over a collection to type a whole run.

param.name: specimen
param.label: Specimen id (leave empty to use the collection element identifier)
param.help: Written to column 1 of the calls table and used as the row id of the HDS sheet later. Empty means: take the element identifier of the BAM, minus a trailing '.bam'.

validator.message: Only letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen are allowed

param.name: source
param.label: Marker reference set
param.help: The bundled set is the one every published number in this port was measured against; supply your own only if you are typing a different panel.
param.option: Bundled CDC Cyclospora set (7 amplicons, 24 PARTs, 78 known haplotypes)

param.name: markers
param.label: Marker (amplicon) FASTA
param.help: The reference the BAM was aligned to. Used only to validate that every BED interval exists in it and lies inside it; no called base is ever taken from it.

param.name: parts
param.label: PART interval BED4
param.help: chrom, start, end, PART name. Column 4 is the PART name.

param.name: known
param.label: Known haplotype FASTA
param.help: Records named <PART>_Hap_<k>. An exact sequence match takes that name; anything else becomes <PART>_NOV_<md5[:6]>.

param.name: min_span
param.label: Spanning reads required to CALL a PART
param.help: Pre-registered value: 50. Below this the PART emits no rows at all, which downstream is read as NOT CALLED (an entirely empty locus block), not as absent. Changing it invalidates the measured concordance.

param.name: min_freq
param.label: Minimum haplotype frequency
param.help: Pre-registered value: 0.05. The denominator is the spanning-read count of the PART, not the sum of the surviving haplotypes.

param.name: min_reads
param.label: Minimum supporting reads per haplotype
param.help: Pre-registered value: 10. Both this and the frequency floor must hold.

param.name: emit_summary
param.label: Also emit the per-PART depth summary
param.help: One row per PART with the spanning depth and whether the PART was called. This is what tells an empty locus block in the sheet apart: dropout (span below the floor) versus called-but-all-haplotypes-gated-out.

tool.help:
**Cyclospora PART haplotype caller** — stage 3a of the LoFreq/PyEuk typing arm.
One marker-aligned BAM in, one long-format calls table out. Map it over a collection of BAMs to type a whole sequencing run.
## Method
There is **no assembly**. Each amplicon is cut into ~100 bp PART intervals by the BED, and an Illumina read is long enough to span a PART end to end, so the haplotype of a PART is just the aligned subsequence of a spanning read; identical subsequences are collapsed and counted.
A read spans `[start, end)` only if its alignment covers every reference position of the interval. Deletions contribute nothing at their positions, insertions are appended in lower case to the preceding reference position (and so change the called length), and secondary / supplementary / unmapped records are skipped.
The BAM is expected to be **already filtered** to MAPQ >= 20 proper pairs by the mapping stage. This tool does not re-apply those filters, exactly like the reference implementation it was ported from.
## Gates — pre-registered, do not tune
| gate | value | meaning | |---|---|---| | spanning reads to call a PART | 50 | below it the PART emits **no rows at all** | | haplotype frequency | 0.05 | of the PART's spanning-read count | | haplotype supporting reads | 10 | both floors must hold |
They are exposed so the tool is honest about what it is doing, not so they can be searched over. The measured concordance against CDC's own calls (precision 0.9150, recall 0.9145 over 153 specimens) holds at these values and at no others.
## The three-state encoding this feeds
A PART with fewer than 50 spanning reads produces **zero rows**, and that becomes an entirely empty locus block in the CDC HDS sheet, which is how the format spells "not called" (amplicon dropout) as opposed to "called, haplotype absent". Nothing downstream can recover the distinction if this tool emits a placeholder row instead, so it does not.
One ambiguity is inherited from that encoding: a PART that *was* called but whose haplotypes all failed the frequency / read floors also produces an empty block. Turn on **the per-PART depth summary** to tell the two apart; it reports the actual spanning depth and the called flag for every PART, including the ones with zero coverage.
## Naming
An exact sequence match against the known-haplotype FASTA takes that record's name. Anything else is named `<PART>_NOV_<md5(seq)[:6]>` and reported as `NOVEL`, with the nearest known haplotype of the same PART and its Levenshtein distance in the `nearest` / `edit` columns. **Those two columns are triage only** — the distance never influences the call, and a novel haplotype is never snapped onto the nearest reference.
## Reference data
The marker FASTA, the PART BED and the 78 known haplotypes are **bundled with the tool**; the default needs no history inputs. Choose *From history* to type a different panel. See the tool's README for why bundling is the default.
## Inputs
- **Marker-aligned BAM** — one specimen, coordinate-sorted, pre-filtered. - **Specimen id** — optional; defaults to the collection element identifier with a trailing `.bam` removed.
## Outputs
- **PART haplotype calls** (tabular, 10 columns): `specimen`, `part`, `span`, `reads`, `freq`, `name`, `match`, `nearest`, `edit`, `seq`. One row per kept haplotype. - **Per-PART depth summary** (optional, tabular, 5 columns): `specimen`, `part`, `span`, `called`, `n_haplotypes`. One row per PART in the BED, including uncovered ones.
-----
Ported from `extract_reads.py` + `call_haplotypes.py` (caller **A**, the direct read-collapse path) of the LoFreq/PyEuk benchmark. Caller B, the LoFreq-informed comparison arm, is deliberately not ported.
